title: Support multi-emotion and multi-target affect updates across StructuredFormats, ResponseParser, ActionInterpreter, and agent-engine.ts

sections.what: Extend turn emotion output from a single scalar/tuple to multi-emotion multi-target impulses and fix ActionInterpreter/agent-engine.ts flattening that corrupts or discards emotion objects.
sections.why: While engine/emotion.py and routes/player_ops.py (handle_map_player_emotions) support 35-dimensional affect updates and schema-fragments.ts line 70 shows memory.emotions dicts, top-level agentAction/agentReact schemas in static/js/shared/json-schemas.ts (lines 56-65, 109, 129) allow only a single {label, intensity, toward} emotion. Worse, static/js/agent/action-interpreter.ts (line 248) runs String(parsed.emotion).trim() on fallback parse (turning objects into '[object Object]'), and static/js/agent-engine.ts (lines 1045, 1140) flattens parsed.emotion to .label before _applyFeltEmotion.
sections.how:
1. Extend EMOTION schema in static/js/shared/json-schemas.ts (lines 56-65, 109, 129) and schema-fragments.ts (lines 71-78) to support an array of {label, intensity, toward} objects (or backward-compatible single object) so characters can express simultaneous mixed or multi-target affect.
2. Update extractEmotion / parseReaction in static/js/agent/response-parser.ts to normalize both single and array emotion outputs.
3. Fix fallback JSON handling in static/js/agent/action-interpreter.ts (line 248, where String(parsed.emotion) destroys objects) and preserve structured emotion objects/arrays instead of stripping to .label in static/js/agent-engine.ts (lines 1045, 1140).
4. Update _applyFeltEmotion in agent-engine.ts (lines 462-475) to iterate and dispatch all parsed affect impulses (preserving opaque player identity per bug-585).
5. Add JS unit tests covering multi-target mixed emotions, ActionInterpreter fallback object preservation, and batch /emotions/map dispatch.
sections.verify: 1. Run npm run build:ts and node tools/unit/run.cjs with tests verifying array and single-object emotion extraction across ResponseParser, ActionInterpreter (including fallback branch), and _applyFeltEmotion.\n2. Verify zero String(object) or '[object Object]' artifacts occur when ActionInterpreter receives structured emotion payloads.

acceptance.text: StructuredFormats (agentAction, agentReact), ResponseParser, and schema-fragments accept multi-emotion / multi-target arrays (e.g. terrified of person A while furious at person B) alongside single-emotion backwards compatibility.

action-interpreter.ts (line 248 fallback) and agent-engine.ts (lines 1045, 1140) no longer coerce emotion objects via String() into '[object Object]' or flatten them to .label strings, preserving intensity and toward metadata.
_applyFeltEmotion in static/js/agent-engine.ts dispatches all distinct emotion impulses (global and target-directed) to /api/players/<name>/emotions/map.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Agent Turn Modal prompt JSON schema examples, Inspector Emotion/Mind tabs, and Agent Lens raw LLM parsing view.

Current availability: static/js/shared/json-schemas.ts constrains emotion to one object; action-interpreter.ts coerces fallback parsed.emotion with String(); agent-engine.ts strips objects to .label before _applyFeltEmotion.

Manual verification steps:
1. Trigger a turn where a character experiences simultaneous contrasting emotions toward two people (e.g. scared of attacker A and furious at betrayer B).
2. Inspect parsed turn output and /api/players/<id>/emotions state.
   - expected: Multiple {label, intensity, toward} impulses survive ResponseParser and ActionInterpreter intact and update both affect dimensions and relationship experiences without '[object Object]' corruption.
